name: create_routine
description: Create a routine in the user's openGym plan (it syncs to all their devices), e.g. "squat 5 × 5 at 100 kg, plank 3 × 60 s, Tuesdays and Fridays". Exercises are matched against the library like log_workout: when a name matches several or none, nothing is saved and `problems` lists candidates to put to the user. Each exercise starts the way picking it in the app starts it; only what you pass is set on top. `weekdays` puts it on those days of the weekly plan, next to whatever is planned there already. Call with dry_run: true first when you interpreted anything, show the preview, and save once the user agrees.

exercise.description: Exercise name as the user said it ("barbell squat"), or an exercise id from search_exercises or an earlier answer (an id never matches the wrong exercise).

sets.description: Number of sets. Omit for the profile's default (3 unless they set their own).

reps.description: Reps per set, for a rep exercise.

seconds.description: Seconds per set, for a hold (plank). Not with reps.

weight.description: Planned load in `unit`; omit or 0 to start from what the user lifted last time.

rest_sec.description: Rest after each set, seconds. 0 or omitted: the global rest timer.

note.description: A note shown with this exercise in the workout.

weekdays.description: The weekdays to plan it on.

unit.description: The unit weights are given in; defaults to the profile's.

name: update_routine
description: Change a routine: rename it, replace its exercise list, append exercises, or move it to other weekdays. Use routine_id from list_routines. `exercises` is the whole new list in order; an exercise named again keeps everything its slot had (rest, warm-ups, progression, notes) except what you pass. `add_exercises` appends. `weekdays` is every day it should be on (it leaves the others); omit it to leave the schedule alone. Pass expected_revision (from get_routine) when the user confirmed a change against what they saw: if the profile moved since, nothing is saved and you get a conflict to read again.
